title: KeyboardShortcutsSheet
wrapsNative: keyboardShortcut(_:modifiers:) on Button and other controls; iPadOS lists the shortcuts while the Command key is held
summary: An app declares its shortcuts with keyboardShortcut, and iPadOS shows them in its own overlay when the Command key is held. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Add keyboardShortcut to the buttons and menu items of the actions people repeat. The title of the control is the name shown in the system's list, so every shortcut needs a control with a title.
whenNotToUse: Do not build a sheet that lists shortcuts, and do not bind a key to open one. Do not reuse the system's shortcuts (Command C, Command H, Command Tab).
api: func keyboardShortcut(_ key: KeyEquivalent, modifiers: EventModifiers = .command) -> some View
func keyboardShortcut(_ shortcut: KeyboardShortcut?) -> some View

states.name: Command held
states.description: On an iPad with a hardware keyboard the system shows the app's shortcuts, grouped by menu, with their titles.

appearance: The system draws the overlay. Nothing in it is themed by Monarch.
platformNotes: The web KeyboardShortcutsSheet is a side sheet opened with "?" that lists groups of shortcuts, can be filtered and shows the Command or Control symbol for the platform. On iOS the list is the system's: holding Command on iPadOS shows every shortcut the visible screen declares, and shortcuts in the app's commands menus (the commands scene modifier) are grouped under their menu. There is nothing to filter or translate; the titles are the controls' own. An iPhone has no such overlay, and shortcuts still work with a connected keyboard. Android shows the system's shortcut helper in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: a shortcut runs the control's action, so it does the same as activating the control with VoiceOver or touch.
System behaviour: a disabled control's shortcut does nothing and is dimmed in the list.
Every shortcut must also be reachable as a visible control or menu item; a shortcut alone cannot be found without a keyboard.
edgeCases: A shortcut works only while its control is in the view tree of the active scene.
Two controls with the same shortcut on one screen: the system picks one. Keep them unique.
Letter keys are matched by the character the layout produces, so a shortcut may sit on another key on a non-US keyboard.

examples.title: From a help button

parityExceptions.reason: Decision: web-only, the platform convention applies. there is no shortcuts sheet with key caps; the system lists shortcuts it finds on the screen (iOS) or in onProvideKeyboardShortcuts (Android), which cannot show sequences such as g then i, or a bare ? key. The labels and groups are listed in order.
